decision: How the Digital Sales Room should treat the third-party marketplace endpoints and third-party custom code for WF-115

state.problem: The WF-115 spec names the builder's Subscription URL, Dynamic filter URL and Action execution URL as POST endpoints, but the research states each is a third-party endpoint the room does not own. The spec also names Custom code (JS) in one extensibility line but never in the data flow. The room must decide how it handles these surfaces.
spec_quotes: The Subscription URL, the Dynamic filter URL and the Action execution URL are all third-party endpoints. The room does not own them. Model them as configuration the builder records, and decide how the room calls them.

The spec does not say the room runs third-party JavaScript. Custom code (JS) and the pause/resume webhook are named in the extensibility line but not in the data flow. Decide whether custom code is in scope and record the decision.
HighLevel POSTs the full trigger config (including targetUrl) to the app's Subscription URL.
The app's Custom Action POSTs execution data to its own API, returns sample-shaped JSON, and HighLevel binds that to custom variables.
constraints: The room is a FastAPI backend over an audited SQLite store; it is not the HighLevel platform.
The room must not make outbound network calls in tests or the demo seed.
A feature page must show something reviewable, so at least one surface must model the inbound direction.
The feature contract requires schema-flexible JSON payloads and no new typed columns.

verdict.instructions: Which treatment should the room take for the third-party URLs and for third-party custom code? Weigh fidelity to the spec, safety of running a test suite with no network, and whether a reviewer can see the behaviour.

criteria.option_a: Record-only configuration plus an inbound delivery model: the room stores the builder's URLs as data, never calls them, exposes no evaluator for custom code, and serves one route that records and evaluates what the platform POSTs to the Subscription URL (eventType in CREATED|UPDATED|DELETED, filters, targetUrl, extras).
criteria.option_b: The room calls the third-party URLs itself, POSTing to the Subscription URL, Dynamic filter URL and Execution URL when a workflow runs.
criteria.option_c: Drop the URL fields and custom code entirely, storing only name, key, filters and sample payload.
criteria.option_d: Run builder custom code (JavaScript) inside the room when an action executes.

reversible.instructions: Is the chosen treatment reversible without changing the stored envelope, so a later workflow can add an outbound caller?

criteria.true: The URLs and code are stored as ordinary JSON, so a caller can be added later without a migration
criteria.false: The choice removes a field a later workflow would need

decision: The review-state machine WF-115 should implement for a marketplace module

state.problem: The spec names a Submit for Review step and an approved/published outcome, and the brief says the review step is a state machine the spec names but does not define. The states must be derived and the derivation recorded.
spec_quotes: Submit for Review with a changelog; version the module; on approval it is available to all sub-accounts.
HighLevel Marketplace review -> published trigger appears in every sub-account's add a trigger menu.
Once approved, the version submitted for review will be published live to all Sub-accounts.
Any workflows using the deleted trigger will skip its execution.
constraints: The brief requires: soft delete, not hard delete, because a deleted trigger's workflows skip execution.
Submission must carry a changelog and increment a version.
A reviewer needs both an approve and a send-back outcome; a terminal refusal is a distinct case.
Every transition must be a validation the tests can exercise.

candidate_state_sets.option_a: Eight stored states: draft, submitted, in_review, changes_requested, approved, published, withdrawn, rejected; deleted derived from the soft-delete timestamp.
candidate_state_sets.option_b: Five stored states: draft, submitted, approved, published, deleted.
candidate_state_sets.option_c: Three stored states: draft, published, deleted.

verdict.instructions: Which state machine best models the review step the spec names? Weigh whether each state has a spec basis or a clear inference, whether a reviewer has the outcomes they need, and whether the set stays small enough to test exhaustively.

criteria.option_a: The eight-state machine with deleted derived from the soft-delete timestamp.
criteria.option_b: The five-state machine with deleted as a stored state.

soft_delete.instructions: Does the chosen machine keep delete as a soft delete whose row survives, so a workflow referencing the key can still be told the trigger was deleted?

criteria.true: Delete sets the deleted timestamp and the row and its key survive for include_deleted reads

decision: Implementation of WF-115 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-115 adds a published app-marketplace workflow for custom triggers and actions. A new domain package, dsr/marketplace_primitives, holds the vocabulary, the validation rules, an eight-state review machine with a soft delete, and a Marketplace service over the audited store, plus a seed. The feature module wf115_publish_custom_workflow_triggers_and_actions.py serves it on /api/wf-115 and is mounted by discovery alone; no shared host file is edited. A frontend feature folder ships a page that authors, reviews, publishes, deletes and restores modules. Two Jev decisions, recorded in orchestration/decisions/wf-115-jev-audit.jsonl, fix that the room records the third-party endpoint URLs as configuration it never calls and never runs custom code, and that the review step is an eight-state machine with deleted derived from the soft-delete timestamp.

declared_unverified: The room never calls the third-party Subscription, Dynamic-filter or Execution URLs, so nothing here proves a real HighLevel delivery resolves as modelled; the delivery route is a model of that payload.
Custom code (JS) is stored, never executed; there is no JavaScript sandbox in the room.
The wf-066 frontend spec fails intermittently under the full parallel frontend run and passes in isolation; it is a file this branch does not touch.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
